newsitem.title: USA: Western Bancorp to acquire Santa Monica Bank.
newsitem.headline: Western Bancorp to acquire Santa Monica Bank.

text.p: Western Bancorp has agreed to acquire Santa Monica Bank for about $198.2 million, the California banking companies said Thursday.

Under the definitive agreement, Santa Monica shareholders can choose to receive either $28 in cash per share, or 0.875 share of Western Bancorp common stock for each of the Santa Monica, Calif.-based bank's share.
If holders of more than 50 percent of Santa Monica's common stock choose to receive Western Bancorp stock, shares and cash will be distributed on a pro rata basis, they said in a joint statement.
If holders of less than 40 percent of the outstanding Santa Monica shares choose to receive stock, all shareholders will receive $28 cash per share at closing.

Santa Monica Bank and Western Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of Western Bancorp, will merge to form a $1.1 billion bank under the name of Santa Monica Bank, operating on the west side of Los Angeles.
Western Bancorp, based in Newport Beach, Calif., will then have two subsidiaries: Santa Monica Bank and National Bank of Southern California.
National Bank will merge into Southern California Bank after Western's previously announced acquisition of its parent, SC Bancorp, is completed.

Upon the expected completion of the merger in January 1998, Western Bancorp will have assets of about $2.1 billion and operate from 34 branches in Orange and Los Angeles counties in southern California.
Western Bancorp's stock rose 50 cents to $32.50 on Nasdaq at midday. Santa Monica Bank climbed $2.56 to $27.06 on the American Stock Exchange.
